plan.contextChunk: This figure is an annotated graph of one full cycle of a transformed sine wave, marked up to expose its midline, amplitude, and period. The vertical y-axis carries ticks from -2 up to 4, the horizontal x-axis is labeled at pi/2 and at pi, and both axes end in arrowheads. The solid dark blue curve leaves the y-axis at height 1, rises to a maximum of 4 a quarter of the way along, falls back through that starting height, bottoms out at -2 near three-quarters of the way, and returns to height 1 at pi. A horizontal orange arrow at the level y = 1 extends rightward from the vertical axis, labeled Midline: y = 1. A vertical teal arrow runs up the curve's peak from that orange level to the maximum, tagged by a leader with Amplitude: |A| = 3. Below the plot, a red double-headed arrow spans the width of the drawn cycle beneath the label Period = pi. The three annotations measure independent things: the vertical center of the oscillation, the stretch away from that center, and the horizontal distance before the shape repeats. Taken together they are the quantities needed to reconstruct the equation of a sinusoid from its picture alone.

interactionPlan.concept: A sinusoid's picture is fully determined by three independent measurements — the midline (vertical center), the amplitude (vertical distance from midline to peak), and the period (horizontal length of one full cycle).
elements: Vertical y-axis with arrowhead, labeled 'y', ticks and numeric labels at -2, -1, 1, 2, 3, 4
Horizontal x-axis with arrowhead, labeled 'x', tick marks at pi/2 and pi with labels 'π/2' and 'π'

Solid dark blue sinusoid curve: starts on the y-axis at y = 1, rises to maximum y = 4 at x = π/4, returns to y = 1 at x = π/2, falls to minimum y = -2 at x = 3π/4, returns to y = 1 at x = π (one full cycle drawn)
Horizontal orange arrow at y = 1 extending rightward from the y-axis, with orange label 'Midline: y = 1'
Vertical teal double-ended/upward arrow from the midline level (y = 1) up to the curve's peak (y = 4) at the maximum
Teal leader line and label 'Amplitude: |A| = 3' pointing at the teal arrow
Red double-headed horizontal arrow beneath the plot spanning x = 0 to x = π
Red label 'Period = π' to the right of the red span arrow
Optional dashed guide lines at the peak level and trough level
Live equation readout of the current curve, e.g. y = 3 sin(2x) + 1

interactions.teaches: Amplitude is the vertical distance from the midline to the peak (and equally down to the trough) — it stretches the wave vertically without moving its center or changing how often it repeats.
interactions.label: Amplitude |A|

interactions.teaches: The midline is a vertical shift: the whole wave slides up or down while the peak-to-midline distance stays exactly the same, so vertical shift and amplitude are separate quantities.
interactions.label: Midline y = D

interactions.teaches: Period is a horizontal repeat length, not a height: squeezing or stretching it changes how much x it takes to complete one cycle while the peak and trough heights never move.
interactions.label: Period (in units of π)

demo_steps.title: The textbook figure
demo_steps.narration: One full cycle of a sine wave centered on the orange line y = 1, reaching up to 4 and down to -2, and repeating after a horizontal distance of π. Three annotations measure three different things.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the amplitude
demo_steps.narration: Drag the teal arrow: the peak climbs to 5 and the trough drops to -3, but the orange midline never moves and the cycle still ends at π. Amplitude is purely the distance from the center line to the extreme.

demo_steps.title: Shrink the amplitude
demo_steps.narration: With a small amplitude the wave hugs the midline. Notice the peak and trough stay symmetric about y = 1 — the midline is always the average of the maximum and minimum.

demo_steps.title: Slide the midline
demo_steps.narration: Now push the orange line down to y = -1. The entire wave travels with it; the gap from midline to peak is unchanged. Vertical shift relocates the wave, amplitude sizes it.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the period
demo_steps.narration: Widen the red span to 2π. The wave needs twice as much horizontal room to finish one cycle, yet the peak and trough heights are untouched — period is a horizontal, not vertical, measurement.

demo_steps.title: Compress the period
demo_steps.narration: Squeeze the span to π/2 and the wave oscillates twice as fast. With midline, amplitude, and period all set, you can read the equation y = A sin(2πx / period) + D straight off the picture.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Midline, amplitude, and period are three independent dials — one moves the wave up and down, one stretches it vertically about that center, and one stretches it horizontally — and together they reconstruct the sinusoid's equation from the picture alone.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Clean white background, thin black axes with arrowheads; y-axis labeled 'y' at top with tick labels -2 through 4, x-axis labeled 'x' at right with ticks and labels at π/2 and π. The sinusoid is a thick dark navy-blue curve drawn for exactly one cycle starting on the y-axis at the midline height, peaking a quarter-cycle in, crossing the midline at the half-cycle, bottoming at three quarters, and returning to the midline at the cycle's end. A horizontal orange arrow sits at the midline level running rightward from the y-axis, labeled in matching orange to the right of the plot as 'Midline: y = D'. A teal vertical arrow rises from the midline to the curve's maximum with a thin black/teal leader arrow pointing to a teal label 'Amplitude: |A| = ...' placed upper right. Below the x-axis a red double-headed arrow spans the drawn cycle, with a red label 'Period = ...' to its right. All three annotation colors (orange midline, teal amplitude, red period) must stay distinct and should visibly track their sliders in real time; show a live equation readout (e.g. y = 3 sin(2x) + 1) near the top so learners connect each slider to its parameter.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for amplitude: the learner drags the teal amplitude handle from the midline to the peak, the peak and trough move farther from or closer to y = 1, and the update shows amplitude as vertical distance from the midline.
- Slider for midline: the learner drags the orange midline arrow up or down, the entire sine wave shifts with it while its height from midline to peak stays fixed, making vertical shift separate from amplitude.
- Slider for period: the learner stretches or compresses the red period span, the wave completes one cycle over the new horizontal distance, showing period as repeat length rather than wave height.

Inspecting the graph, we can determine that the period is π, the midline is y=1, and the amplitude is 3. See the figure.

A graph of y=3sin(2x)+1. The graph has an amplitude of 3. There is a midline at y=1. There is a period of pi. Local maximum at (pi/4, 4) and local minimum at (3pi/4, -2).

discrepancies: The generated figure adds a colour-coded live equation readout ('y = 3 sin(2x) + 1') at the top-right that does not exist in the source figure.
Y-axis tick range extends to −3 (extra tick/label below the source's −2 bottom tick), so the vertical extent is slightly larger than the source.

The leader line from the 'Amplitude: |A| = 3' label is a long, nearly horizontal line spanning most of the plot width, whereas the source uses a short diagonal arrow from the label to the peak region — it visually cuts across empty plot space.

The annotation labels sit in a fixed right-hand column well clear of the curve; in the source 'Midline: y = 1' is horizontally adjacent to the orange arrowhead and 'Period = π' sits directly right of the red span, giving a tighter composition.
Source shows the curve's opening value tick marks along the x-axis only at π/2 and π regions; the generated figure draws four quarter-cycle ticks (extra unlabeled ticks at π/4 and 3π/4).
evaluation.notes: A close, correctly coloured reproduction of the annotated sinusoid with excellent, pedagogically meaningful interactions (three sliders, a six-step narrated player, and hotspot popups); minor deviations are an added equation readout, an extra −3 tick, and a long awkward leader line to the amplitude label.

feedback.rationale: No failure modes or action items were flagged, concept and interactivity are strong, and the remaining deviations are trivial cosmetic differences that do not warrant another iteration.
